notable_absence.finding: Thin, config-field-catalog page as expected by the batch's own framing - most of its content is the variable table and one full example JSON payload, with almost no prose beyond template-type description (Standard vs Advanced). Kept concepts/relations minimal per the batch instructions rather than forcing ontology out of a reference table.

cross_component_finding: Confirms the payload field set only ever surfaces 'critical' or 'warning' - never 'info' - consistent with monitoring:event's triggersAlert relation (Info-severity events never trigger an alert, so they never reach a payload). This page's variable table (alert.name/severity/alertDuration/alertDetectedAt/description; tenant.tenantId/tenantName; project.projectId/projectName; resource.clusterId/clusterName/appServiceId/appServiceName/regionProvider/capellaResourceUrl) is identical, field for field, to microsoft-reference.md's own table, differing only in message-card wrapper (Slack Block Kit here vs Microsoft Adaptive Cards there) - both use the same monitoring:alert-payload data model. webhook-reference.md's payload, by contrast, uses an entirely different field-naming scheme (see webhook-reference.json), so the 'one shared model' picture applies to Slack and Microsoft Teams specifically, not to all three integrations uniformly - direct evidence for this batch's hypothesis question about whether integrations share one configuration model.
